sections.title: Stroke Iskemik vs Hemoragik

content.text: ISCHEMIC STROKE: BP management follows permissive hypertension principles unless >220/120 mmHg or specific indications exist. Antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel) for secondary prevention. Statins for atherosclerotic disease. Avoid anticoagulation in acute phase. HEMORRHAGIC STROKE: Aggressive BP lowering (target <140/90). Reverse anticoagulation if present. Neurosurgical consultation for cerebellar hematoma >3cm, hydrocephalus, or clinical deterioration. ICP management with osmotherapy.

sections.title: Komplikasi dan Perawatan Keperawatan

content.text: Common post-stroke complications include deep vein thrombosis (DVT), aspiration pneumonia, pressure sores (decubitus), joint contractures, spasticity, depression, shoulder subluxation, and nutritional deficiencies. Nursing care includes proper positioning every 2 hours, range of motion (ROM) exercises, joint mobilization, and contracture prevention. Physical therapy should begin as early as medically feasible.

sections.title: Disfagia, Nutrisi, dan Manajemen Eliminasi

content.text: DYSPHAGIA ASSESSMENT: All stroke patients must have swallowing assessment before any oral intake. Bedside water swallow test: give 1 teaspoon of cold water, observe for coughing, wet voice, or delayed swallow. If failed, NGT feeding is required. NUTRITION: Enteral nutrition via NGT if dysphagia present. Target 25-30 kcal/kg/day. Monitor for aspiration. BOWEL MANAGEMENT: Prevent constipation with adequate hydration, fiber, and regular bowel regimen. BLADDER MANAGEMENT: Assess for urinary retention; intermittent catheterization if needed; avoid indwelling catheter if possible.

Manajemen kandung kemih: katerisasi intermiten, hindari kater permanen
Never give oral intake before swallowing assessment - aspiration pneumonia is a leading cause of death in stroke patients

sections.title: Manajemen Koma

content.text: Coma management follows Brain Trauma Foundation (BTF) guidelines. HEAD POSITIONING: Elevate head of bed 30 degrees. Keep head midline to optimize cerebral venous drainage. Avoid neck flexion or rotation. ICP MONITORING: Maintain ICP <20 mmHg. CPP (Cerebral Perfusion Pressure) should be maintained at 60-70 mmHg. Calculate as MAP - ICP. SEDATION: Use propofol or midazolam for ICP control. Avoid hypotension. OSMOTHERAPY: Mannitol 0.25-1 g/kg IV or hypertonic saline 3% for elevated ICP. SEIZURE PROPHYLAXIS: Phenytoin or levetiracetam for first 7 days post-TBI. GLUCOSE MANAGEMENT: Maintain normoglycemia (80-180 mg/dL). TEMPERATURE: Prevent fever; treat aggressively if present.
CPP = MAP - ICP; maintaining CPP 60-70 mmHg is critical to prevent secondary brain injury
